correctness.rationale: For h=f times conjugate(g) in exact H3, the intrinsic gradient pairing is (Δ_S+24)h/2, so the mixed integrand is (I+Δ_S/42)h. Harmonic decomposition of products leaves only degrees 0, 2, 4, 6; the multipliers are respectively 1, 6/7, 11/21 and 0. For the converse, the zonal-square expansion has coefficients 8/49 and 6/49 in degrees 2 and 4. Varying the zone axis annihilates the two moment functions separately by orthogonality; the addition formula then gives every claimed moment. The antipodal design equivalence follows, and positivity of the normalized weights supports the Parseval-frame interpretation. A separately written exact check, independent_exact_check.py, tested the zonal identity, icosahedral even moments and the projector identity for the six-axis Gram. Its C=2I−AᵀA and AAᵀ=2I give three eigenvalues 7/3 for S0 and four zeros; the mixed identity gives S1=7I/4−3S0/4 and the unique mixture. The frozen verify.py was inspected, not run; the exact check did not separately compute a tangential-gradient matrix.

value.rationale: Repairing singular sample values by tangential measurements is a meaningful problem, and the reported mathematics is correct. But the arbitrary-node test is a direct degree-three, first-channel specialization of the indexed channel identities and span lemma, and the purported sharp extra example is recovered from the known cap Gram by its standard first-order expansion. Neither part supplies a remaining distinct invariant, construction or boundary for acceptance.
